chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from one of his companions who said:

A man from his companions used to visit Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), but he was absent for a time not performing Hajj. So one of his acquaintances came to him and said to him, 'So-and-so, what happened to him?' He began to lay down the speech, thinking that he meant wealth and the world. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'How is his religion?' He said, 'As you love.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, it is the richness.'

key_terms.الْمَيْسَرَة: Wealth, affluence, or ease in life
key_terms.يُضَجِّعُ الْكَلَامَ: Laying down the speech, speaking in a drawn-out or explanatory manner

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean when he says a person's religion is safe because of their wealth?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies 'wealth' (al-ghina) as the defining characteristic of a companion’s religious safety, countering the assumption that his long absence was due to worldly distraction. Shia scholars interpret this not merely as material affluence, but as 'spiritual sufficiency' or contentment (qana'ah), which shields the believer from the anxieties and compromises that often accompany poverty or desperate need. This highlights the practical implication that financial stability can serve as a protective shield for piety, allowing one to focus on worship without the distraction of survival struggles.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from one of his companions who said,

‘A man from his<sup>asws</sup> used to come over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, but he was absent for a time not performing Hajj. So one of his acquaintances came over to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘So and so, what happened?’ So he went on laying down the speech, thinking that he, rather, had become rich, the affluent, and the worldly. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How is his Religion?’ So he said, ‘Just as you<sup>asws</sup> love’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! It is the richness’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from certain individuals of his people who has said the following:

“A man, of the companions of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) would very often attend the gathering with the Imam. He remained absent for a certain time and did not attend Hajj also. Once a certain individual of his people who knew him came in and the Imam asked, ‘How so and so is doing?’ The narrator has said that the man then began to speak of him in very short expressions thinking that he meant thereby wealth and the world. Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then asked, ‘How is his religion?’ He said, ‘It is just as you love.’ The Imam said, ‘That, by Allah, is wealth.’”
